messages:
marta: FYI hitting a weird one in prod — structured output schema rejections are being swallowed when requests hit the proxy fallback path. Console shows 200, but no fncall telemetry and no schema reject count in the dashboard.

alex: Can you paste an example request/response? sounds like a logging gap on the proxy.

marta: short logs: 
```
REQ id=abc123 model=redwood-v2 proxy=enabled prompt=...
RESP status=200 body="{\"text\":\"sorry\"}"
validator: rejection=nil (route=proxy-fallback)
```
This one should have been a `schema_reject` but shows as success.

jia: Is it only proxy-fallback or also routing to cheaper variants? We added a fast-path that coerces non.json to text for latency SLOs. Might be masking structured errors.

sam: This is bad for customers using structured tool-calls — they rely on a 4xx-ish surface. If they're getting 200 with text we silently lose the tool invocation. We should treat structured-validate failures as non-transient and surface them.

alex: Two angles: 1) short-term: emit a metric from the proxy when validator would have rejected but we coerced, e.g. `proxy.structured_coerce_count` with dimensions (route, model, customer). 2) long-term: change fallback behavior to return a `structured_validation_error` envelope instead of coercing. Both need console/dashboard changes.

marta: Agreed. Right now the rollback is subtle because rate dashboards don't show rejects and retries inflate token usage. Customer hit a huge bill spike yesterday.

jia: Telemetry note: validators live in the runtime service; proxy currently doesn't call them before coercion. We can either call the validator synchronously (adds latency) or run a fast checksum heuristic and async-report rejected examples. I prefer async-reporting + sampling to avoid high cardinality.

sam: For quota accounting we need to decide: should coerced attempts count as normal token usage or be refunded? If we change behavior customers will see a different cost pattern. Might need to coordinate billing.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by @alex: patch/proxy-emit-metric v1 -> canary in eng-stage at 2026-02-18T15:12:00Z

alex: Plan: push metric emission first (non-blocking), add a `schema_coerce` tag to requests, then iterate. If we see >0.5% coercions for a customer, pause auto-fallback and surface a banner in console. Thoughts?

marta: Banner is great. Also add a per-customer sampling of rejected payloads blob (PII-scrub) to S3 for triage.

jia: Implementation detail: metric + sampled payloads should include `validator_reason` and `validator_snippet` but we must scrub APIs/keys. I'll add a small scrubber lib.

sam: UX: Console needs a dedicated row in per-route metrics: `Structured rejects (coerced / surfaced)` and a toggle to `enforce_strict_schema` for enterprise customers.

alex: +1. I'll open a console ticket and tag @product. Short-term action items: (1) alex -> emit metric & sampling (canary) (2) jia -> scrubber + async reporting (3) marta -> create dashboard tile and banner copy (4) sam -> cost/billing spike playbook.

infra-bot: Canary deployment started: proxy-metrics-canary -> 10% traffic (region-us-west). Rollout ETA 20m.

marta: Thanks. If we see a spike in `proxy.structured_coerce_count` we'll pause canary. Please log any related customer support threads to #support quickly. :thumbsup:

alex: Will post follow-up with PR links and metric IDs.

sam: Leaving a reminder to revisit quota semantics in the next infra sync.

jia: I'll have the scrubber PR up in ~3h.

marta: Great — assigning follow-ups in linear. Closing the loop in this thread once canary completes.
